q-342851.name: Question 1
q-342851.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & ={(-{x}^{3}+4x\sqrt{x})}^{′} \\  & ={(-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{3/2})}^{′} \\  & =3(-{x}^{2})+\frac{3}{2}(4{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =-3{x}^{2}+6{x}^{1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{″}(x) & ={(-3{x}^{2}+6{x}^{1/2})}^{′} \\  & =2(-3x)+\frac{1}{2}(6{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =-6x+3{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =-6x+\frac{3}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the second derivative at $x=1$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{″}(1) & =-6(1)+\frac{3}{\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-6+3 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first derivative, we have g′(x)=(−x3+4xx)′=(−x3+4x3/2)′=3(−x2)+32(4x1/2)=−3x2+6x1/2. Computing the second derivative, we have g″(x)=(−3x2+6x1/2)′=2(−3x)+12(6x−1/2)=−6x+3x−1/2=−6x+3x.

Finally, evaluating the second derivative at x=1, we obtain g″(1)=−6(1)+31=−6+3=−3.

q-10892.name: Question 2
q-10892.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-7)}^{′} &  \\  & =3\cdot 2{x}^{2}+2\cdot 4x-0 \\  & =6{x}^{2}+8x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & ={(6{x}^{2}+8x)}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot 6x+8 \\  & =12x+8\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the second derivative at $x=-2$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-2) & =12(-2)+8 \\  & =-24+8 \\  & =-16.\end{aligned}
$$

q-342877.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{6{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-8}{2x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}+x-4{x}^{-1}) \\  & =6x+1+(-1)(-4{x}^{-2}) \\  & =6x+1+4{x}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x+1+4{x}^{-2}) \\  & =6+0+(-2)(4{x}^{-3}) \\  & =6-\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-104295.name: Question 5
q-104295.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{5-{x}^{4}}{6{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{6{x}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5}{6{x}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5}{6}{x}^{-2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}{x}^{-3}-\frac{x}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{5}{3}{x}^{-3}-\frac{x}{3}) \\  & =5{x}^{-4}-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{-4}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =-20{x}^{-5} \\  & =-\frac{20}{{x}^{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$
